subject: Enhancement: Installing RRO on Ubuntu 14.04 should set it up to use previously installed libs

messages.author: 98bef3acb3d81c90
messages.subject: Enhancement: Installing RRO on Ubuntu 14.04 should set it up to use previously installed libs
parts:
I've been running R 3.1.1 on Ubuntu 14.04 LTS 64-bit for quite some time and have quite a bit of libs installed in /usr/local/lib/R/site-library/.

Just installed RRO and found out that it is only seeing the libs in "/usr/lib64/RRO-8.0/R-3.1.1/lib/R/library", for example:

$ R

R version 3.1.1 (2014-07-10) -- "Sock it to Me"

Platform: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (64-bit)

R is free software and comes with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY.
You are welcome to redistribute it under certain conditions.
Type 'license()' or 'licence()' for distribution details.

  Natural language support but running in an English locale

Type 'demo()' for some demos, 'help()' for on-line help, or

Type 'q()' to quit R.

Error in library(setwidth) : there is no package called ‘setwidth’
> library(dplyr)
Error in library(dplyr) : there is no package called ‘dplyr’
> library(ggplot2)
Error in library(ggplot2) : there is no package called ‘ggplot2’
> library(ggmap)
Error in library(ggmap) : there is no package called ‘ggmap’
> .libPaths()
[1] "/usr/lib64/RRO-8.0/R-3.1.1/lib/R/library"
> .libPaths(c(.libPaths(), "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"))
> library(dplyr)

Attaching package: ‘dplyr’

The following objects are masked from ‘package:stats’:

    filter, lag

The following objects are masked from ‘package:base’:

    intersect, setdiff, setequal, union

I know that I can set .libPaths() in my ~/.Rprofile or in Rprofile.site, but I think you might want to try and detect that and give the option to automagically update the appropriate config file to avoid errors like the ones pointed above.

Might also help to avoid the reinstallation of packages that are already there (in my case, knitr, markdown, stringr, formatR, digest, evaluate and mime)

> update.packages(repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com")
